values.note: 2026: electric sites (1-13) $25/night, $17 with an Interagency Senior/Access Pass; primitive sites 14-18 (paved parking, no electricity, no lengths posted) and walk-in tent sites 19-21 $20, $12 with the pass. First-come sites are cash or check only.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232006 (notice '2026 Camping Fees Electric Sites (1-13): $25 per night or $17 with Interagency Senior/Access Pass Primitive & Walk-In Sites (14-21): $20 per night or $12 with Interagency Senior/Access Pass', 'cash/check only; no credit cards accepted'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Only sites 7-12 are reservable on recreation.gov, 'up to 2 days in advance'; if not reserved they go first come, first served like sites 1-6 and 13-21. A reserved site must be occupied by 2 p.m. the day after arrival or it is cancelled. Check-in 2 p.m., out by noon.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232006 (notice 'Sites 1-6 and 13-21 are first-come, first-served ... Sites 7-12 are reservable online at recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232006 up to 2 days in advance. If not reserved, they are first-come, first-served', 'You must occupy your reserved site by 2:00 pm the day following your arrival date'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: 13 electric sites with paved pads: site 1 42 ft, 2 47, 3 50, 4 38, 5 55, 6 46, 7 51, 8 35, 9 36, 10 31, 11 42, 12 29, 13 24. Five primitive sites (14-18) with paved parking and three walk-in tent sites (19-21).

sites.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232006 (notice 'The campground has 21 campsites', 'Site lengths are as follows: Site 1 is 42 feet ... Site 13 is the shortest at 24 feet', 'Sites accommodate vehicles from 24 ft to a maximum of 55 ft'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Four flush restrooms with sinks plus accessible vault toilets; three water spigots and hand pumps; the camp store sells firewood and ice. No showers, dump station, Wi-Fi or cell service.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232006 (Facilities: 'accessible vault toilets and non-accessible flush toilets. Hand pumps and a drinking fountain with faucet are available. The camp store sells firewood and ice'; notice 'Restrooms: 4 flush restrooms', 'Water Access: 3 water spigots', 'Wi-Fi: Not available', 'Showers/Dump Station: Not available', 'Cell Service: None'), read 2026-10-21

discounts.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232006 (notice '$25 per night or $17 with Interagency Senior/Access Pass'), read 2026-10-21

summary: Confirmed on recreation.gov (campground description and the 2026 notice): $25 electric sites ($17 with the Senior/Access pass; $20 primitive/walk-in), 21 sites with 13 paved electric pads 24-55 ft, 15/30/50-amp, flush and vault toilets, spigots, camp store (firewood/ice), no showers/dump/Wi-Fi. Booking changed to some_sites: only sites 7-12 reservable, up to 2 days ahead. Fees changed 22-25 -> 25 (the $22 was a rate-table line; the notice states $25). Not stated: season (staffed May 13 - Sep 14, 2026; rec.gov rate seasons only), water/sewer at the site. Note unchanged.
flags: Missing phone: recreation.gov gives (304) 801-3262 for local staff May 13 - Sep 14, 2026 and (304) 478-2481 (Cheat-Potomac RD, Parsons) otherwise.

Missing agency website: no Forest Service page found (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/horseshoe-recreation-area-campground returns 'Page not found'); the recreation.gov page is the only official one.

Note vs pages: the --AWH-style note says 'along a remote section of the Cheat River'; recreation.gov says the campground 'is tucked in a valley along Horseshoe Run' (Horseshoe Creek), about 7 miles from St. George. Left for AWH (note marked '-AWH').

Waterfront re-audit lead (weak): recreation.gov invites 'relaxing beside the creek' and names Horseshoe Creek 'a designated snorkel site'; the entry is 'not waterfront'. Not a claim that sites are on the water.
